cards.text: First Chronicles opens with one giant family tree, and it starts at the very top with Adam, the first man (1 Corinthians 15:45). No stories, no speeches, just names, from Adam down through Enoch and Methuselah to Noah and his three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth. It's like the book walked in, skipped the hello, and started reading the guest list.
First come the families of Japheth, then Ham, one people after another. Partway through Ham's family, the list stops on one name: Nimrod, son of Cush.

cards.question: The family list stops to say one thing about Cush's son Nimrod. What is it?

answers.text: He began to be a mighty one on the earth
He was the first to call on the LORD
He went down to Egypt in a famine

cards.text: Then the list keeps going with Mizraim's peoples, including the Casluhites, from whom the Philistines came, and Canaan's peoples, like the Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites. Next come the families of Shem, and down his line, Eber has two sons, and the first one gets a name with a reason attached.

cards.question: Why is Eber's son named Peleg?

answers.text: Because in his days the earth was divided
Because in his days the rivers flooded
Because in his days the famine ended

cards.text: Peleg's brother Joktan gets a long list of sons all his own. Peleg, meanwhile, gets one line about the earth being divided. Imagine your whole life story fitting in one headline.
Then the list runs one line straight from Shem: Arphaxad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor and Terah. And it lands on a name you KNOW: Abram, that is, Abraham. FINALLY.

Abraham's sons are Isaac and Ishmael. The list gives Ishmael's twelve sons, starting with his firstborn, Nebaioth, and then six sons born to Keturah, Abraham's concubine, Midian among them. Twelve sons, friend. I had six cookie cutter kids on that counter and still called them by the wrong name half the time.

Then Isaac's sons: Esau and Israel, the man also called Jacob (Genesis 32:28). The list follows Esau's family, Amalek among them, and then the family of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36:20). That's a LOT of cousins, friend. You'd need a whole group chat just to plan the cookie exchange.
Esau is also called Edom (Genesis 36:1), and now the list turns to the kings who reigned in the land of Edom.

cards.question: These kings reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites.

cards.text: First comes Bela son of Beor, and when Bela dies, Jobab reigns in his place. When Jobab dies, Husham reigns in his place, and after him comes Hadad son of Bedad.

cards.question: In the list of Edom's kings, Hadad son of Bedad lost a battle to Midian in the country of Moab.

cards.text: After him the pattern keeps going: a king dies and someone reigns in his place, through Samlah, Shaul and Baal-hanan to another king named Hadad. Then that Hadad dies, and the list ends with the chiefs of Edom. Adam to Edom in ONE chapter, friend. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer and moved maybe two inches.
